content.comment_body: Hello. I'm based in the UK and currently developing a system for use in Germany. I'm working with [product_name] [version_no] along with an [product_name] display. When I add the status from a softkey into a message for control via the display, it always shows 'On' or 'Off'. However, I need it to show 'Ein' or 'Aus'. I've tried setting both the display and [product_name] programming software languages to German, and even reinstalled the software in German, but the softkey status is always shown as 'On/Off', both in the hardware and simulation. Using numeric values like 1 or 0 is an alternative, but it's not ideal. The only way to display 'Ein/Aus' is to assign them to the status display object in message properties, but then you can't actually set the softkey via the display. Are there any solutions for this? I find it surprising that developers in Germany would have to accept 'On/Off' text on these displays. Thank you for your attention.
The status text shown for a softkey is fixed as 'On/Off' and isn't configurable. This is one of the areas where [company_name] often lags behind in implementing such changes.
Thanks for clarifying. While it doesn't resolve my issue, at least I now understand the product limitations.

With this display, you have keys F1 through F4. It might help to use these keys to change things like the status of a pulse relay at the TRG input. You can enable retentivity if needed, and the status can be displayed with any custom text up to 8 characters. This allows you to change up to four pulse relays in a single message and have the message active only in setup mode. Using AND logic blocks with the key and active message is recommended; otherwise, the keys could change the status without proper user insight.

Thank you for your idea. Unfortunately, F1-F4 keys are already assigned to other features in my setup, so implementing this would require substantial redesign. Still, I appreciate your suggestion and will consider it further.

You might not need the attached file, but it's a simple example. For your scenario, handling multiple messages with the same keys could be more challenging. With a spare digital input, you can create a setup switch—like in the example using I1. Alternatively, a menu using an up/down counter could be applied, with the counter activating the appropriate message. Note, though, this will need more logic blocks.
Thanks for sending the example file. I'll review it next week when I have more time, and I'm sure it'll give me helpful ideas. Much appreciated.

analysis.insight_summary: The main issue is that the softkey status text on the [product_name] display remains fixed as 'On/Off', regardless of changing all related language settings to German on both the display hardware, programming software, and PC. This design limits localization, posing difficulties for developers targeting non-English regions, and has led to user frustration. While some workarounds exist, such as alternative programming approaches, these often require significant modifications or do not fully resolve the language display concerns.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the product to support complete language localization, specifically so that softkey status text on the display can appear as 'Ein/Aus' when the system language is set to German.
